Analyses for "Animal-pollinated plants are more temporally variable than wind-pollinated plants" by Lana G. Bolin, Kamren Decker, Sharon Y. Strauss, and Jennifer A. Rudgers.

# Setup

Load libraries and data
```{r, message=F, warning=F}
# Clear environment
rm(list = ls())

# Load libraries
libraries <- c("magrittr", "lme4", "car", "emmeans", "MuMIn", "sjPlot", "ape",  "phytools", "googlesheets4", "brms", "reshape2", "DHARMa", "ggeffects", "tidybayes", "posterior", "phytools", "ggtree", "nlme")
invisible(lapply(libraries, require, character.only = T))
library(tidyverse)

# Set plot theme
theme_set(theme_bw() +
            theme(
              plot.background = element_blank()
              ,panel.grid.major = element_blank()
              ,panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
              ,panel.background = element_blank()
              ,axis.text.x  = element_text(vjust=0.5, size=10)
              ,axis.text.y  = element_text(vjust=0.5, size=10)
            ))

# Load the dataset
data.2004 <- read.csv("./data/sp_interactions_stability_data.csv")
```

Prep data
```{r}
# Calculate species_CV for each species in each quad, and remove species that were never observed
data.2004 %<>%
    mutate(biomass.sum = apply(.[(10:29)], 1, sum, na.rm=T),
           species_mu = apply(.[(10:29)], 1, mean, na.rm=T),
           species_sd = apply(.[(10:29)], 1, sd, na.rm=T),
           species_CV = species_sd/species_mu) %>%
    filter(biomass.sum > 0)

# Sum the biomass for each species across all sites and quadrats within each year. This has 1 row per species, and a column for each year.
yearsums.2004 <- data.2004 %>% 
  group_by(kartez) %>%
  summarise(across(c(X2004, X2005, X2006, X2007, X2008, X2009, X2010, X2011, X2012, X2013, X2014, X2015, X2016, X2017, X2018, X2019, X2020, X2021, X2022, X2023), sum, na.rm=T))

# Count the number of years each species has non-zero biomass across the SEV. Add as column to yearsums
yearsums.2004$n.nonzero.years <- rowSums(yearsums.2004[, 2:21] != 0)

# Filter to years with at least 3 years of non-zero biomass
ThreePlus.2004 <- yearsums.2004 %>%
  filter(n.nonzero.years >=3) 

data.2004 %<>%
  filter(kartez %in% ThreePlus.2004$kartez)
```


Data summaries
```{r}
# Number of species
length(unique(data.2004$kartez))

# Number of sites, and quads per site. 4 ecosystems (the 4 core sites) and 2 ecotones (grass-grass and grass-shrub). 
data.2004 %>% group_by(site) %>% summarise(n.quads = length(unique(quad_ID)))

# Number of quads
length(unique(data.2004$quad_ID))



# Number of species with data for each species interaction
data.2004 %>%
  distinct(kartez, Pollination.new) %>%
  group_by(Pollination.new) %>%
  summarise(n = n())

data.2004 %>% 
  distinct(kartez, Dispersal.new) %>%
  group_by(Dispersal.new) %>%
  summarise(n = n())

# Number of annuals vs. perennials
data.2004 %>% 
  distinct(kartez, LifeHistory) %>%
  group_by(LifeHistory) %>%
  summarise(n = n())

# Breakdown of pollination strategy by annual/perennial 
LHxPol <- data.2004 %>% 
  distinct(kartez, LifeHistory, Pollination.new) %>%
  filter(kartez %in% data.2004$kartez) %>%
  group_by(LifeHistory, Pollination.new) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
LHxPol

  # % of annuals that are animal-pollinated 
  LHxPol[[1, 3]]/(LHxPol[[1, 3]] + LHxPol[[2, 3]]) * 100
  
  # % of perennials that are animal-pollinated
  LHxPol[[4, 3]]/(LHxPol[[4, 3]] + LHxPol[[5, 3]]) * 100
  
# Breakdown of dispersal strategy by annual/perennial
LH.Disp <- data.2004 %>% 
  distinct(kartez, LifeHistory, Dispersal.new) %>%
  group_by(LifeHistory, Dispersal.new) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
LH.Disp

  # % of annuals that are animal-dispersed 
  LH.Disp[[1, 3]]/(LH.Disp[[1, 3]] + LH.Disp[[2, 3]]) * 100
  
  # % of perennials that are animal-dispersed 
  LH.Disp[[4, 3]]/(LH.Disp[[4, 3]] + LH.Disp[[5, 3]]) * 100

# Breakdown of pollination strategy by grass/non-grass
FG.Pol <- data.2004 %>% 
  distinct(kartez, FunctionalGroup, Pollination.new) %>%
  group_by(FunctionalGroup, Pollination.new) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
FG.Pol
  
# Breakdown of dispersal strategy by grass/non-grass
FG.Disp <- data.2004 %>% 
  distinct(kartez, FunctionalGroup, Dispersal.new) %>%
  group_by(FunctionalGroup, Dispersal.new) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
FG.Disp
  
  # % of grasses that are animal-dispersed
  FG.Disp[[4, 3]]/(FG.Disp[[4, 3]] + FG.Disp[[5, 3]]) * 100

  # % of non-grasses that are animal-dispersed
  (FG.Disp[[1, 3]] + FG.Disp[[6, 3]])/(FG.Disp[[1, 3]] + FG.Disp[[2, 3]] + FG.Disp[[6, 3]] + FG.Disp[[7, 3]]) * 100

# How many species had genus-level pollination data?
data.2004 %>%
  group_by(kartez) %>%
  filter(row_number() == 1) %>%
  group_by(PollinationGS) %>%
  summarise(n = n())

# How many species had genus-level dispersal data?
data.2004 %>%
  group_by(kartez) %>%
  filter(row_number() == 1) %>%
  group_by(DispersalGS) %>%
  summarise(n = n())

# How many families are in the dataset?
families <- data.2004 %>%

nrow(families)
```

Prep data for brms models
```{r}
PIC.data <- data.2004 %>%
  # Remove space from all species names
  mutate(taxon.new = str_remove_all(taxon.new, " ")) %>% 
  # Fix Opuntia macrocenta typo
  mutate(taxon.new = ifelse(taxon.new == "Opuntia_macrocenta", "Opuntia_macrocentra", taxon.new)) %>%
  # Remove taxa ending in "_NA"
  filter(!grepl("_NA$", taxon.new))
```


How much of the total plant biomass in the system is represented by the focal set?  
```{r}
mass <- read.csv("./data/sev331_quadrat_plant_species_biomass.csv")

# Make unique quad_ID
mass$quad_ID <- as.factor(
      paste(
        mass$site,
        mass$web,
        mass$transect,
        mass$treatment,
        mass$block,
        mass$plot,
        mass$subplot,
        mass$quad,
        sep = "_"))

# Filter to the same years, quads, season, and sites
mass.filt <- mass %>% 
  filter(year %in% 2004:2023) %>%
  filter(quad_ID %in% data.2004$quad_ID) %>%
  filter(season == "fall") %>%
  filter(site %in% data.2004$site)

# Focal set total biomass
focal.sum <- sum(data.2004$biomass.sum)

# Total biomass of all plants
total.sum <- sum(mass.filt$biomass.BM)

# Percent of total biomass represented by our focal set
focal.sum / total.sum * 100
```



# Plant temporal variability models

## Main model

```{r, message=F}
# Scale latitude and longitude
data.2004 %<>%
  mutate(X_sc = scale(X),
         Y_sc = scale(Y))

# Pollination (Table S1)
mod.pol <- lmer(species_CV ~ Pollination.new + X_sc + Y_sc + (1|kartez), na.action = na.omit, data = data.2004 %>% filter(kartez != "CHER2")) # CHER2 only has family-level pollination data 
Anova(mod.pol, type = 2)

# Dispersal (Table S6)
mod.disp <- lmer(species_CV ~ Dispersal.new + X_sc + Y_sc + (1|kartez), na.action = na.omit, data = data.2004)
Anova(mod.disp, type = 2)


### Effect sizes (% increase for animal-pollinated or -dispersed)

# Pollination
pol.emm <- summary(emmeans(mod.pol, pairwise ~ Pollination.new))
(pol.emm$emmeans[1, 2] - pol.emm$emmeans[2, 2]) / pol.emm$emmeans[2, 2] * 100

# Dispersal
disp.emm <- summary(emmeans(mod.disp, pairwise ~ Dispersal.new))
(disp.emm$emmeans[1, 2] - disp.emm$emmeans[2, 2]) / disp.emm$emmeans[2, 2] * 100


### Plot marginal effect of each predictor

## Pollination

# Get predictions
pred_pol <- ggpredict(mod.pol, terms = "Pollination.new")

# Figure 1A
Pol.new.plot <- ggplot(pred_pol, aes(x = x, y = predicted, color = x)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
                width = 0.05) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("A", "W"),
    labels = c("Animal", "Wind")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("A" = "red", "W" = "blue"),
    labels = c("A" = "Animal", "W" = "Wind")
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "Temporal variability (biomass CV)",
    x = "Pollination strategy",
    color = "Pollination"
  ) +
  ylim(c(2.75, 3.7)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
Pol.new.plot


## Dispersal

# Get predictions
pred_disp <- ggpredict(mod.disp, terms = "Dispersal.new")

# Figure 1B
Disp.new.plot <- ggplot(pred_disp, aes(x = x, y = predicted, color = x)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
                width = 0.05) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("A", "W"),
    labels = c("Animal", "Wind")
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("A" = "darkgreen", "W" = "orange"),
    labels = c("A" = "Animal", "W" = "Wind")
  ) +
  labs(
    y = "Temporal variability (biomass CV)",
    x = "Dispersal strategy",
    color = "Dispersal"
  ) +
  ylim(c(2.75, 3.7)) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
Disp.new.plot
```

## Prep bee data

Bee data sites: B = Blue grama grassland, C = Creosote shrubland, G = Black grama grassland
```{r}
# Filter to fall season (months 7-10) 
bee.data.filt <- bee.data %>% filter(month %in% c(7:10))

# Melt into standard long format
bee.melt <- melt(bee.data.filt, id.vars = c("month", "year", "start_date", "end_date", "complete_sampling_month", "complete_sampling_year", "ecosystem", "transect", "direction", "color"),
                 value.name = "count", variable.name = "species_code", na.rm = TRUE, factorsAsStrings = TRUE)


### Calculate Area under curve for abundance

# Collapse to transect-level monthly abundance
bee_transect_month <- bee.melt %>%
  group_by(year, ecosystem, transect, species_code, month) %>%
  summarise(
    count = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# AUC function, based on the trapezoidal rule to get area under curve (AUC)
calculate_auc <- function(data) {
  data <- data %>% arrange(month)

  if (nrow(data) < 2) return(NA_real_)

  sum(
    diff(data$month) *
      (head(data$count, -1) + tail(data$count, -1)) / 2,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
}

# Apply AUC within each year × species × transect
bee_auc <- bee_transect_month %>%
  group_by(year, ecosystem, transect, species_code) %>%
  summarise(
    auc = calculate_auc(pick(month, count)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


### Remove rare species

# Cast data so there is a column for each year, and a row for each species x ecosystem. This sums across transects in each year x ecosystem
bee.wide <- dcast(bee_auc, species_code + ecosystem ~ year, sum, value.var = "auc", fill=0)

# Number of years each bee species has non-zero abundance
bee.yearsums <- bee.wide %>%
  group_by(species_code) %>%
  summarise(across(3:19, ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))

# Count the number of years each species has non-zero biomass across the SEV
bee.yearsums$n.nonzero.years <- rowSums(bee.yearsums[, 2:18] != 0)

# Filter to years with <3 years of non-zero abundance
bee.less3 <- bee.yearsums %>%
  filter(n.nonzero.years < 3) 

# Filter out species with fewer than 3 non-zero years
bee.wide %<>%
  filter(!species_code %in% bee.less3$species_code)


### Calculate bee_CV as CV of max abundance over time, for each ecosystem
bee.wide %<>%
  mutate(sum = apply(.[(3:20)], 1, sum, na.rm=T),
           species_mu = apply(.[(3:20)], 1, mean, na.rm=T),
           species_sd = apply(.[(3:20)], 1, sd, na.rm=T),
           species_CV = species_sd/species_mu) %>%
  filter(!is.na(species_CV)) 
```



## Prep rodent data 

Use analagous pipeline to bees
```{r}
### Filtering steps

# Exclude squirrels, chipmunks, and seed carnivores
rodent.data %<>%
  dplyr::select(-c("AMIN", "AMLE", "CHIN", "MUMU", "MUMU", "OTVA", "REME", "REMO", "REXX", "SIHI", "SPSP", "ONAR", "ONLE", "ONXX")) %>%
  filter(habitat %in% c("Black grama grassland", "Creosote shrubland")) %>%
  filter(season_fs == "fall")

# Filter to habitats to compare to bees, and web_id asspatial unit
rodent.data2 <- rodent.data %>%
  filter(habitat %in% c("Black grama grassland", "Creosote shrubland")) %>%
  dplyr::select(year, habitat, web_id, DIME:PGFV)  

# Melt to long format
rodent.melt <- melt(
  rodent.data2,
  id.vars = c("year", "habitat", "web_id"),
  value.name = "animals.trap.night",
  variable.name = "species_code",
  na.rm = TRUE,
  factorsAsStrings = TRUE
)

# Restrict to same years as bees
rodent.melt <- rodent.melt %>%
  filter(year %in% 2002:2019)


### Calculate yearly mean abundance for each species in each web. This is the rodent analogue of yearly bee abundance per transect
rodent.web.year <- rodent.melt %>%
  group_by(species_code, year, habitat, web_id) %>%
  summarise(
    mean.animals = mean(animals.trap.night, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


### Remove rare species

# Cast to wide format, summing across webs within each ecosystem-year
rodent.wide <- dcast(
  rodent.web.year,
  species_code + habitat ~ year,
  value.var = "mean.animals",
  fun.aggregate = sum,
  fill = 0
)

# Count number of nonzero years across ecosystems combined, by species
rodent.yearsums <- rodent.wide %>%
  group_by(species_code) %>%
  summarise(across(`2002`:`2019`, ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop")

rodent.yearsums$n.nonzero.years <- rowSums(rodent.yearsums[, as.character(2002:2019)] != 0)

# Filter out species with fewer than 3 non-zero years
rodent.less3 <- rodent.yearsums %>%
  filter(n.nonzero.years < 3)

rodent.wide <- rodent.wide %>%
  filter(!species_code %in% rodent.less3$species_code)


### Calculate mean, SD, and CV across years the same way as bees
rodent.wide <- rodent.wide %>%
  mutate(
    sum = rowSums(across(`2002`:`2019`), na.rm = TRUE),
    species_mu = rowMeans(across(`2002`:`2019`), na.rm = TRUE),
    species_sd = apply(dplyr::select(., `2002`:`2019`), 1, sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    species_CV = species_sd / species_mu
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(species_CV))


### Rename columns and levels to match bee data

# Rename habitat to ecosystem to match bee data
rodent.wide <- rodent.wide %>%
  rename(ecosystem = habitat)

# Recode ecosystem names to match bee data
rodent.wide <- rodent.wide %>%
  mutate(
    ecosystem = dplyr::recode(
      ecosystem,
      "Black grama grassland" = "G",
      "Creosote shrubland" = "C"
    ),
    ecosystem = factor(ecosystem, levels = c("G", "C"))
  )

bee.wide <- bee.wide %>%
  mutate(ecosystem = factor(ecosystem, levels = c("G", "C", "B")))
```

How many bee and rodent species do we have?
```{r}
# Bee
n_distinct(bee.wide$species_code)

# Rodent
n_distinct(rodent.wide$species_code)
```



## Combine data

```{r}
# Add a column to rodent data saying it's a rodent. Same for bee data.
rodent.wide$species_type <- "rodent"
bee.wide$species_type <- "bee"

# Merge 
rodent.bee.data <- rbind(rodent.wide, bee.wide)

# Filter to ecosystems present in both bee and rodent data
rodent.bee.data %<>% filter(ecosystem != "B")

# Replication
rodent.bee.data %>%
  group_by(ecosystem, species_type) %>%
  summarise(n = n())
```


## Fit model

```{r}
# Table S8
bm.noB.ln.mod.cov <- lmer(log(species_CV) ~ species_type + ecosystem + (1 | species_code), data = rodent.bee.data)
Anova(bm.noB.ln.mod.cov)


### Effect sizes (% increase in bee variability) 

# marginal means for species_type, averaging over ecosystem
emm_species <- emmeans(bm.noB.ln.mod.cov, ~ species_type)

# Bees are 35% more variable than rodents
contrast(emm_species, method = "pairwise", type = "response")

### Plot

# convert emmeans to a data frame
emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_species)

# back-transform for plotting
emm_df <- emm_df %>%
  mutate(
    species_CV = exp(emmean),
    lower_CL = exp(lower.CL),
    upper_CL = exp(upper.CL)
  )

# Figure 2
bee.rodent.plot <- ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = species_type, y = species_CV)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_CL, ymax = upper_CL), width = 0.1) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Bees", "Rodents")) +
  labs(
    x = "Interaction type",
    y = "Temporal variability (abundance CV)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(color = "black")
  )
bee.rodent.plot
```

Subsampling / rarefaction to offset the 10x more bees than rodents
```{r}
set.seed(423)

# Make sure rodent is the reference level
rodent.bee.data <- rodent.bee.data %>%
  mutate(species_type = relevel(factor(species_type), ref = "rodent"))

# Main model using full dataset
bm.noB.ln.mod.cov <- lmer(
  log(species_CV) ~ species_type + ecosystem + (1 | species_code),
  data = rodent.bee.data
)

# Number of rodent rows to match
n_rodents <- sum(rodent.bee.data$species_type == "rodent")

# Repeatedly subsample bees to match rodents, then refit model
results <- replicate(1000, {
  
  bees_sub <- rodent.bee.data %>%
    filter(species_type == "bee") %>%
    slice_sample(n = n_rodents)
  
  dat_sub <- bind_rows(
    bees_sub,
    rodent.bee.data %>% filter(species_type == "rodent")
  ) %>%
    mutate(species_type = relevel(factor(species_type), ref = "rodent"))
  
  mod <- lmer(
    log(species_CV) ~ species_type + ecosystem + (1 | species_code),
    data = dat_sub
  )
  
  fixef(mod)["species_typebee"]
})

# Convert log-scale effects to bee:rodent CV ratios
ratio_results <- exp(results)

# Mean % more variable
(exp(mean(results)) - 1) * 100

# 95% interval
(exp(quantile(results, c(0.025, 0.975))) - 1) * 100



### Plot distribution on original ratio scale

# Convert log-scale effects to bee:rodent CV ratios
coef_main_ratio <- exp(fixef(bm.noB.ln.mod.cov)["species_typebee"])

# Convert log-scale effects to bee:mammal CV ratios
ratio_results <- exp(results)

df_plot <- data.frame(ratio = exp(results))

# Figure S5
subsample_plot <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = ratio)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "grey70", color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = coef_main_ratio, color = "red", linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    x = expression("Bee : rodent " * italic(CV) * " ratio"),
    y = "Frequency"
  )

subsample_plot
```


# Phylogenetic signal

## Prep the data and the tree for phylo signal test

Prep tree
```{r}
# Load tree with original branch lengths from Zanne tree
tree.orig <- read.tree("./data/phylo_tree/orig.tre")

# Plot tree
plotTree(tree.orig)

# Check if tree and data have the same species 
intersect(unique(PIC.data$taxon.new), tree.orig$tip.label)
setdiff(unique(PIC.data$taxon.new), tree.orig$tip.label)
setdiff(tree.orig$tip.label, unique(PIC.data$taxon.new)) 

# Remove "Grusonia_clavata" and "Munroa_squarrosa" from PIC.data because they are missing from the tree
PIC.data %<>% filter(!taxon.new %in% c("Grusonia_clavata", "Munroa_squarrosa"))

# Resolve multifurcations with branches of zero length
tree.orig.mult <- multi2di(tree.orig)
```

Prep data 
```{r}
# Change binary variables to 0 and 1 (for pollination & dispersal: 0 = wind, 1 = animal)
PIC.data %<>%
  mutate(Pollination.num = ifelse(Pollination.new == "W", 0, 1),
         Dispersal.num = ifelse(Dispersal.new == "W", 0, 1)) 

# Each taxon will be one row for PICs, so take the mean CV for each species
data.pics.means <- PIC.data %>%
  group_by(taxon.new) %>%
  summarise(cv.mean = mean(species_CV, na.rm=T),
            Pollination.num = mean(Pollination.num, na.rm=T),
            Dispersal.num = mean(Dispersal.num, na.rm=T)) %>%
  data.frame()

# Row names are taxa, in same format as tree
row.names(data.pics.means) <- data.pics.means$taxon.new 
```


## Test for phylogenetic signal in temporal variability

```{r}
# Column in data.pics.means that matches tree$tip.label
taxon_col <- "taxon.new"   

# Named trait vector (names must match tree tip labels) 
cv <- data.pics.means$cv.mean
names(cv) <- data.pics.means[[taxon_col]]

# keep only taxa shared by tree and data
keep <- intersect(tree.orig.mult$tip.label, names(cv))
cv2 <- cv[keep]
tree2 <- drop.tip(tree.orig.mult, setdiff(tree.orig.mult$tip.label, keep))

# remove NAs if present
ok <- !is.na(cv2)
cv2 <- cv2[ok]
tree2 <- drop.tip(tree2, setdiff(tree2$tip.label, names(cv2)))

# Calculate lambda
cv_lambda <- phylosig(tree2, cv2, method = "lambda", test = TRUE)
cv_lambda
```


# brms models

```{r}
# Construct a covariance matrix of species
A.init.orig <- ape::vcv.phylo(tree.orig.mult)

# Save and read in phylogenetic data
phylo_list_init_orig <- list(A.init.orig = A.init.orig)
dput(phylo_list_init_orig, "phylo_list_init_orig.txt")
phylo_list_init_orig_r <-dget("phylo_list_init_orig.txt")

# z-score Lat and Long
PIC.data %<>%
  mutate(Latitude_z = scale(X),
         Longitude_z = scale(Y))
```

## Pollination

Output suppressed for run time. Delete "eval=F" to run.
```{r, eval=F}
brms.mod.orig.pol <- bf(species_CV ~ (1|Pollination.new) + Latitude_z + Longitude_z + (1|site) + (1|gr(taxon.new, cov = A.init.orig)))
brms.mod.orig.pol

# Set priors for pollination model
prior.pol <- c(
            set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 1)", class = "sd", group = "Pollination.new"), 
            set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "b", coef = "Latitude_z"),
            set_prior("normal(0, 0.5)", class = "b", coef = "Longitude_z"),
            set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 1)", class = "sd", group = "site"),
            set_prior("student_t(3, 0, 1.5)", class = "sd", group = "taxon.new")
            )
prior.pol

# Run the model
k_fit_brms.pol <- brm(brms.mod.orig.pol, 
                  data = PIC.data, data2 = phylo_list_init_orig_r,
                  family = "gaussian", prior = prior.pol,
                  chains = 4, cores = 8, iter = 2000, backend = "cmdstanr",
                  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.999, max_treedepth = 14)) # step_size = 0.01

# Save model to disk and reload it in the next chunk so you only have to fit the brms model once.
saveRDS(k_fit_brms.pol, file = "k_fit_brms_pol.rds")
```

Analyze model
```{r}
# Load model from disk

# Get summaries

summary(k_fit_brms.pol, prob = 0.5) 

plot(k_fit_brms.pol)

### Model checking plots. Posterior predict.

# Full group level estimates for random effects
ranef(k_fit_brms.pol, groups = "Pollination.new", probs = c(0.025, 0.975)) 
ranef(k_fit_brms.pol, groups = "site", probs = 0.95)

  )

halfeye_pol_mains
```

# Make phylogenetic trees with temporal variability and species interaction traits mapped on

Make a dataframe for plotting the tree
```{r}
# Get mean CV for each species. 
new.pic.data.summary <- PIC.data %>%
  group_by(kartez) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            mean.cv = mean(species_CV, na.rm=T))

# Join with species interaction data
phylo.data <- left_join(new.pic.data.summary, PIC.data %>% dplyr::select(kartez, Pollination.new, Dispersal.new, taxon.new), by = "kartez") %>% 
  group_by(kartez) %>% 
  filter(row_number()==1) %>% data.frame()

# ASFE2 is "Astragalus_feensis"
phylo.data$taxon.new[phylo.data$kartez == "ASFE2"] <- "Astragalus_feensis"

# Change "taxon.new" to "label" for merge with tree data below
colnames(phylo.data)[6] <- "label"

# Row names as genus species
rownames(phylo.data) <- phylo.data$label

# Remove columns I don't need
phylo.data$kartez <- NULL
phylo.data$n <- NULL
```


```{r, warning=F}
library(ggnewscale)

# Create a circular ("fan") phylogeny
p <- ggtree(tree.orig, layout="fan") 

# Extract only the genus from each species name for tip labels
tree.orig$tip.label.genus <- sub("_.*", "", tree.orig$tip.label)

# ggtree stores both tip and internal nodes in p$data, so pad the genus vector with NAs so that its length matches the number of rows in p$data
toAppend <- nrow(p$data) - length(tree.orig$tip.label)

tree.orig$tip.label.genus <- append(tree.orig$tip.label.genus, rep(NA, toAppend))

# Add genus names to the ggtree data object
p$data$tip.label.genus <- tree.orig$tip.label.genus


# Extract x- and y-coordinates of the tips (species) only. These coordinates will be used to position additional points
tip_positions <- p$data %>%
  filter(isTip) %>%
  dplyr::select(label, x, y)

# Merge tip coordinates with species metadata (CV, pollination, dispersal)
tip_data_merged <- tip_positions %>%
  left_join(phylo.data, by = "label")

# Add genus labels to the tree tips
p <- p + geom_tiplab(aes(label = tip.label.genus), size = 2) + # tip labels on tips
  xlim(0, max(tip_positions$x) + 220)   # extend plot space for dots

# Add a ring of points representing mean species CV
p1 <- p +
  geom_point(data = tip_data_merged,
             aes(x = x + 220, y = y, color = mean.cv),
             size = 2) +
  scale_color_gradient(low  = "grey90",
                       high = "grey10",
                       name = "Biomass CV") +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_color()

# Add a ring of points representing pollination strategy
p.pol <- p1 +
  geom_point(data = tip_data_merged,
             aes(x = x + 190, y = y, color = Pollination.new),
             size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("W" = "blue", "A" = "red"),
                     name = "Pollination strategy",
                     labels = c("Animal", "Wind")) +
  theme_tree2()

# Pollination: Figure 1C
p.pol


# Add a ring of points representing dispersal strategy
p.disp <- p1 +
  geom_point(data = tip_data_merged,
             aes(x = x + 190, y = y, color = Dispersal.new),
             size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("W" = "darkgreen", "A" = "orange"),
                     name = "Dispersal strategy",
                     labels = c("Animal", "Wind"),
                     na.value = "transparent") +
  theme_tree2()

# Dispersal: Figure 1D
p.disp
```





# CCM 

Use Elijah’s pairs of plant-bee species, and do CCM to see if bee abundance predicts plant abundance.

Plants:
* Cactaceae (visited by 29 bee species)
* Larrea tridentata (visted by 54 bee species)
* Sphaeralcae (visted by 46 bee species)

```{r}
# Load Table S1 from Clark et al Ecosphere submission
bee_diets <- read.csv("./data/bee_diet_breadth_table.csv")

# Create a table for each plant species, that includes the bees that feed on it
cactaceae_bees <- bee_diets %>%
  filter(str_detect(Floral.partner.s., "Cactaceae"))

larrea_bees <- bee_diets %>%
  filter(str_detect(Floral.partner.s., "Larrea tridentata"))

sphaeralcea_bees <- bee_diets %>%
  filter(str_detect(Floral.partner.s., "Sphaeralcea"))

bee_plant_links <- bind_rows(
  cactaceae_bees %>%
    mutate(plant_group = "Cactaceae"),

  larrea_bees %>%
    mutate(plant_group = "Larrea tridentata"),

  sphaeralcea_bees %>%
    mutate(plant_group = "Sphaeralcea")
)
```

Prep plant data
```{r}
# Make a plant_group column for my 3 plant groups
mass %<>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    plant_group = case_when(
      family == "Cactaceae" ~ "Cactaceae",
      genus == "Larrea" & sp.epithet == "tridentata" ~ "Larrea tridentata",
      genus == "Sphaeralcea" ~ "Sphaeralcea",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Restrict to the 3 sites in bee data
mass_bee_sites <- mass %>%
  filter(site %in% c(
    "core_blue",
    "core_creosote",
    "core_black"
  )) %>%
  mutate(
    ecosystem = case_when(
      site == "core_blue"      ~ "B",
      site == "core_creosote"  ~ "C",
      site == "core_black"     ~ "G"
    )
  )

# Create the census windows (start, end, mid)
census_dates <- mass_bee_sites %>%
  group_by(year, season, ecosystem) %>%
  summarise(
    census_start = min(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    census_end   = max(date, na.rm = TRUE),
    census_mid   = census_start + (census_end - census_start) / 2,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Add census windows to mass_bee_sites
mass_bee_sites %<>%
  left_join(
    census_dates,
    by = c("year", "season", "ecosystem")
  )

### Calculate abundance of the three plant groups. Fill with zeros when unobserved in a quad.

# Which quads were actually sampled
sampled_quads <- mass_bee_sites %>%
  distinct(
    year,
    season,
    ecosystem,
    site,
    quad_ID
  )

# Create all 3 plant groups for every sampled quadrat
plant_groups <- c(
  "Cactaceae",
  "Larrea tridentata",
  "Sphaeralcea"
)

sampled_quads <- sampled_quads %>%
  crossing(
    plant_group = plant_groups
  )

# Calculate observed biomass
plant_quad <- mass_bee_sites %>%
  filter(!is.na(plant_group)) %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    season,
    ecosystem,
    site,
    quad_ID,
    plant_group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    plant_biomass = sum(biomass.BM, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Join biomasses to the complete set of sampled quads
plant_quad <- sampled_quads %>%
  left_join(
    plant_quad,
    by = c(
      "year",
      "season",
      "ecosystem",
      "site",
      "quad_ID",
      "plant_group"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    plant_biomass = replace_na(plant_biomass, 0)
  )


### Get seasonal biomass for each plant group (mean biomass across all sampled quadrats)
plant_season <- plant_quad %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    season,
    ecosystem,
    plant_group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_plant_biomass = mean(plant_biomass),
    n_quads = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    census_dates,
    by = c("year", "season", "ecosystem")
  )
```

Prep bee data
```{r}
# Turn bee data into long format. We're keeping all months of data for now. Get start, end, and mid dates of sampling, like with plant data
bee_long <- bee.data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(
      month,
      year,
      start_date,
      end_date,
      complete_sampling_month,
      complete_sampling_year,
      ecosystem,
      transect,
      direction,
      color
    ),
    names_to = "species_code",
    values_to = "count",
    values_drop_na = TRUE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    start_date = as.Date(start_date),
    end_date = as.Date(end_date),
    sample_mid = start_date + (end_date - start_date) / 2
  )
```

Checks
```{r}
# Temporal coverage
plant_season %>%
  group_by(ecosystem, season) %>%
  summarise(
    first_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year),
    n_years = n_distinct(year),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Restrict plant data to 2002-2019, to match bee data
plant_season %<>%
  filter(year >= 2002, year <= 2019)

# Spatial coverage - no Larrea tridentata in Blue
plant_season %>%
  group_by(ecosystem, plant_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_year_seasons = n(),
    n_nonzero = sum(mean_plant_biomass > 0),
    proportion_nonzero = mean(mean_plant_biomass > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


```

Quick and dirty analysis without any phenological information: annual abundance of bees known to visit this plant → future plant biomass
```{r}
# 1. Calculate annual abundance for each bee species
bee_annual <- bee_long %>%
  filter(
    !year %in% c(2016, 2017),
    species_code %in% bee_plant_links$Code
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    ecosystem,
    species_code
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    annual_abundance = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 2. Turn each bee species into a boom/bust index: Standardize each bee species within ecosystem
bee_annual <- bee_annual %>%
  group_by(ecosystem, species_code) %>%
  mutate(
    bee_z = as.numeric(scale(annual_abundance))
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. Create one bee index for each plant group
bee_plant_annual <- bee_annual %>%
  inner_join(
    bee_plant_links,
    by = c("species_code" = "Code")
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    ecosystem,
    plant_group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    bee_index = mean(bee_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_bee_species = n_distinct(species_code),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 4. Use spring plant biomass (to start)
plant_spring <- plant_season %>%
  filter(
    season == "spring",
    year >= 2002,
    year <= 2023
  ) %>%
  select(
    year,
    ecosystem,
    plant_group,
    mean_plant_biomass
  )

plant_future <- plant_spring %>%
  transmute(
    future_year = year,
    ecosystem,
    plant_group,
    plant_biomass_future = mean_plant_biomass
  )

# 5. Create 1-, 2-, and 3-year datasets
lagged_data <- bee_plant_annual %>%
  crossing(lag = 1:3) %>%
  mutate(
    future_year = year + lag
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    plant_future,
    by = c(
      "future_year",
      "ecosystem",
      "plant_group"
    )
  )

# And add plant biomass in year t
lagged_data <- lagged_data %>%
  left_join(
    plant_spring %>%
      rename(
        plant_biomass_t = mean_plant_biomass
      ),
    by = c(
      "year",
      "ecosystem",
      "plant_group"
    )
  )

# 6. Remove the Larrea × blue-grama combination (Because Larrea has zero biomass throughout B)
lagged_data <- lagged_data %>%
  filter(
    !(ecosystem == "B" &
        plant_group == "Larrea tridentata")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(plant_biomass_future),
    !is.na(plant_biomass_t)
  )

# 7. First look: just plot it
ggplot(
  lagged_data,
  aes(
    x = bee_index,
    y = plant_biomass_future
  )
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    plant_group ~ lag,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Bee boom/bust index",
    y = "Future spring plant biomass"
  ) 

ggplot(
  lagged_data,
  aes(
    x = bee_index,
    y = log1p(plant_biomass_future)
  )
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    plant_group + ecosystem ~ lag,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Bee boom/bust index",
    y = "log(1 + future spring plant biomass)"
  ) 


# Quick model
models <- lagged_data %>%
  mutate(
    log_biomass_future = log1p(plant_biomass_future),
    log_biomass_t = log1p(plant_biomass_t)
  ) %>%
  group_by(plant_group, ecosystem, lag) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ broom::tidy(
      lm(
        log_biomass_future ~ log_biomass_t + bee_index,
        data = .x
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

models %>%
  filter(term == "bee_index") %>%
  select(
    plant_group,
    ecosystem,
    lag,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# Test whether bee booms predict subsequent plant biomass within ecosystems, while estimating one common bee effect from all ecosystems
models_pooled <- lagged_data %>%
  mutate(
    log_biomass_future = log1p(plant_biomass_future),
    log_biomass_t = log1p(plant_biomass_t)
  ) %>%
  group_by(plant_group, lag) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ broom::tidy(
      lm(
        log_biomass_future ~
          log_biomass_t +
          bee_index +
          factor(ecosystem),
        data = .x
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

models_pooled %>%
  filter(term == "bee_index") %>%
  select(
    plant_group,
    lag,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)


# Verify that this isn't just one or two bizarre years driving the Sphaeralcea result
sph1 <- lagged_data %>%
  filter(
    plant_group == "Sphaeralcea",
    lag == 1
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    log_biomass_future = log1p(plant_biomass_future),
    log_biomass_t = log1p(plant_biomass_t)
  )

m_sph1 <- lm(
  log_biomass_future ~ log_biomass_t + factor(ecosystem),
  data = sph1
)

sph1$plant_residual <- residuals(m_sph1)

ggplot(
  sph1,
  aes(
    x = bee_index,
    y = plant_residual,
    label = year
  )
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(
    aes(shape = ecosystem),
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    nudge_y = 0.03,
    size = 3
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Sphaeralcea-associated bee boom/bust index",
    y = "Future Sphaeralcea biomass\n(after accounting for current biomass and ecosystem)"
  )
```

So we have a promising result for Sphaeralcea.  

Now let's try adding climate to models, to see if a wet year causes high bee abundance in year t and high plant abundance in year t+1
```{r}
### Fix bee-plant links first

# Make a clean link table (no diet breadth)
bee_plant_links_clean <- bee_plant_links %>%
  distinct(Code, plant_group)

# Rebuild annual bee index
bee_plant_annual <- bee_annual %>%
  inner_join(
    bee_plant_links_clean,
    by = c("species_code" = "Code"),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    ecosystem,
    plant_group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    bee_index = mean(bee_z, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_bee_species = n_distinct(species_code),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


### Rebuild lagged plant-bee dataset

lagged_data <- bee_plant_annual %>%
  crossing(lag = 1:3) %>%
  mutate(
    future_year = year + lag
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    plant_future,
    by = c(
      "future_year",
      "ecosystem",
      "plant_group"
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    plant_spring %>%
      rename(
        plant_biomass_t = mean_plant_biomass
      ),
    by = c(
      "year",
      "ecosystem",
      "plant_group"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !(ecosystem == "B" &
        plant_group == "Larrea tridentata"),
    !is.na(plant_biomass_future),
    !is.na(plant_biomass_t)
  )


### Add precipitation

precip <- mass_bee_sites %>%
  distinct(
    year,
    season,
    ecosystem,
    season.precip
  )

# Check that there is one precipitation value per group
precip %>%
  count(year, season, ecosystem) %>%
  count(n)

# Put spring and fall precipitation in separate columns
precip_wide <- precip %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = season,
    values_from = season.precip,
    names_prefix = "precip_"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    precip_t = precip_spring + precip_fall
  )

# Add precipitation during bee year t
lagged_data_climate <- lagged_data %>%
  left_join(
    precip_wide %>%
      select(
        year,
        ecosystem,
        precip_t
      ),
    by = c("year", "ecosystem")
  )

# Add spring precipitation in future response year
lagged_data_climate <- lagged_data_climate %>%
  left_join(
    precip_wide %>%
      select(
        future_year = year,
        ecosystem,
        precip_future_spring = precip_spring
      ),
    by = c(
      "future_year",
      "ecosystem"
    )
  )


### Climate-adjusted lagged models

models_climate <- lagged_data_climate %>%
  mutate(
    log_biomass_future = log1p(plant_biomass_future),
    log_biomass_t = log1p(plant_biomass_t),

    precip_t_z =
      as.numeric(scale(precip_t)),

    precip_future_spring_z =
      as.numeric(scale(precip_future_spring))
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    plant_group,
    lag
  ) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ broom::tidy(
      lm(
        log_biomass_future ~
          log_biomass_t +
          bee_index +
          precip_t_z +
          precip_future_spring_z +
          factor(ecosystem),
        data = .x
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()


### Look at bee effects

models_climate %>%
  filter(term == "bee_index") %>%
  select(
    plant_group,
    lag,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

```

So the pattern is now: years with unusually high abundance of Sphaeralcea-associated bees are associated with higher Sphaeralcea biomass one year later, even after controlling for current Sphaeralcea biomass, precipitation in year t, spring precipitation in the response year, and ecosystem.

The other groups do not show that pattern. Cactaceae actually has a negative lag-2 association (β = -0.672, P = 0.0395), which is opposite the original hypothesis, and Larrea is inconsistent.

Let's test whether the Sphaeralcea lag-1 effect is robust to individual bee species. The simplest useful test is leave-one-bee-species-out: rebuild the Sphaeralcea bee index 45 times, each time excluding one species, and refit the same precipitation-controlled model.
```{r}
### Leave-one-bee-species-out analysis for Sphaeralcea

sph_bees <- bee_plant_links_clean %>%
  filter(plant_group == "Sphaeralcea") %>%
  pull(Code) %>%
  unique()

length(sph_bees)
# should be 45


# Function that removes one bee species, rebuilds the index,
# and fits the Sphaeralcea lag-1 model
leave_one_bee_out <- function(bee_to_remove) {

  # Recalculate Sphaeralcea bee index without this species
  bee_index_loo <- bee_annual %>%
    filter(
      species_code %in% sph_bees,
      species_code != bee_to_remove
    ) %>%
    group_by(year, ecosystem) %>%
    summarise(
      bee_index = mean(bee_z, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Replace original Sphaeralcea bee index
  dat <- lagged_data_climate %>%
    filter(
      plant_group == "Sphaeralcea",
      lag == 1
    ) %>%
    select(-bee_index) %>%
    left_join(
      bee_index_loo,
      by = c("year", "ecosystem")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      log_biomass_future = log1p(plant_biomass_future),
      log_biomass_t = log1p(plant_biomass_t),
      precip_t_z = as.numeric(scale(precip_t)),
      precip_future_spring_z =
        as.numeric(scale(precip_future_spring))
    )

  # Fit same model
  fit <- lm(
    log_biomass_future ~
      log_biomass_t +
      bee_index +
      precip_t_z +
      precip_future_spring_z +
      factor(ecosystem),
    data = dat
  )

  # Return bee effect
  broom::tidy(fit) %>%
    filter(term == "bee_index") %>%
    mutate(
      bee_removed = bee_to_remove
    )
}


### Run it for all 45 bees

sph_loo <- purrr::map_dfr(
  sph_bees,
  leave_one_bee_out
)


### Examine results

sph_loo %>%
  arrange(estimate) %>%
  select(
    bee_removed,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# The Sphaeralcea lag-1 result is not being driven by any single bee species. Good!
sph_loo %>%
  summarise(
    min_beta = min(estimate),
    median_beta = median(estimate),
    max_beta = max(estimate),
    min_p = min(p.value),
    median_p = median(p.value),
    max_p = max(p.value),
    n_positive = sum(estimate > 0),
    n_p_lt_05 = sum(p.value < 0.05)
  )
```

Look at annual vs. perennial Sphaeralcea species
```{r}
sphaeralcea_species <- mass_bee_sites %>%

# All species are perennial
sphaeralcea_species %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# We want to ask whether the lag-1 relationship occurs in S. hastulata, S. polychroma, or both
### Species-level Sphaeralcea spring biomass

sph_species <- c(
  "Sphaeralcea hastulata",
  "Sphaeralcea polychroma"
)

# All sampled spring quadrats
sph_sampled_quads <- mass_bee_sites %>%

# Biomass of each species in each quadrat

# Fill sampled quadrats where species was absent with zero

# Mean biomass across sampled quadrats

### Sphaeralcea bee index

sph_bee_index <- bee_plant_annual %>%

### Current and next-year species biomass

### Add precipitation

# Let's test whether bee abundance in year t predicts Sphaeralcea occupancy in spring of t+1

### Sphaeralcea occupancy by ecosystem and year

sph_occupancy <- plant_quad %>%

# Model

  occupancy_future ~

broom::tidy(m_sph_occupancy) %>%
```

# New analysis testing if Sphaeralcea-associated bee abundance predicts Sphaeralcea biomass

Note, the uses some steps from the previous analysis, so don't delete everything in "CCM"

Step 1: Find the best bee abundance window
Step 2: Fit the biomass model

Prep data
```{r}
# First, let's check sampling coverage. We're missing coverage in 2016 and 2017, so let's exclude those intially.
bee.data %>%
  group_by(year, ecosystem) %>%
  summarise(
    n_months = n_distinct(month),
    n_complete_months = n_distinct(
      month[complete_sampling_month == 1]
    ),
    first_date = min(as.Date(start_date)),
    last_date = max(as.Date(end_date)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# Identify bees recorded visiting Sphaeralcea
sph_bee_codes <- bee_plant_links_clean %>%
  filter(plant_group == "Sphaeralcea") %>%
  pull(Code) %>%
  unique()

# Check that all bee codes exist in the abundance dataset
setdiff(sph_bee_codes, names(bee.data))

# Calculate total associated-bee abundance per sampling record
bee_sph <- bee.data %>%
  filter(
    !year %in% c(2016, 2017),
    complete_sampling_month == 1
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    bee_count = rowSums(
      across(all_of(intersect(sph_bee_codes, names(bee.data)))),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),
    window = case_when(
      month %in% 3:5 ~ "early",
      month %in% 6:8 ~ "mid",
      month %in% 9:10 ~ "late"
    )
  )

# Calculate abundance per sampling record for each window
bee_seasonal <- bee_sph %>%
  filter(!is.na(window)) %>%
  group_by(year, ecosystem, window) %>%
  summarise(
    bee_abundance = mean(bee_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_bees = sum(bee_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_records = sum(!is.na(bee_count)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate full-season abundance
bee_full <- bee_sph %>%
  group_by(year, ecosystem) %>%
  summarise(
    bee_abundance = mean(bee_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_bees = sum(bee_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_records = sum(!is.na(bee_count)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(window = "full")

# Combine windows
bee_windows <- bind_rows(
  bee_seasonal,
  bee_full
)


# Check missing counts - looks good
bee_sph %>%
  summarise(
    n_records = n(),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(bee_count)),
    proportion_missing = mean(is.na(bee_count))
  )

# Examine sampling effort by window - looks good
bee_windows %>%
  group_by(window) %>%
  summarise(
    min_records = min(n_records),
    median_records = median(n_records),
    max_records = max(n_records),
    min_abundance = min(bee_abundance),
    max_abundance = max(bee_abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Step 1: Find the best bee abundance window
```{r}
# 1. Construct the modeling dataset

# Spring Sphaeralcea biomass
sph_plant <- plant_season %>%
  filter(
    plant_group == "Sphaeralcea",
    season == "spring"
  ) %>%
  select(
    year, ecosystem,
    mean_plant_biomass
  )

# Pair current and next-year biomass
sph_pairs <- sph_plant %>%
  rename(biomass_t = mean_plant_biomass) %>%
  mutate(future_year = year + 1) %>%
  left_join(
    sph_plant %>%
      transmute(
        future_year = year,
        ecosystem,
        biomass_future = mean_plant_biomass
      ),
    by = c("future_year", "ecosystem")
  )

# Join bee windows and precipitation
sph_model_data <- bee_windows %>%
  inner_join(
    sph_pairs,
    by = c("year", "ecosystem")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    precip_wide %>%
      select(year, ecosystem, precip_t),
    by = c("year", "ecosystem")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    precip_wide %>%
      transmute(
        future_year = year,
        ecosystem,
        precip_future_spring = precip_spring
      ),
    by = c("future_year", "ecosystem")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    log_biomass_future = log1p(biomass_future),
    log_biomass_t = log1p(biomass_t),
    log_bees = log1p(bee_abundance)
  )

# Keep only observations with complete data in all four windows
complete_pairs <- sph_model_data %>%
  group_by(year, ecosystem) %>%
  filter(
    n_distinct(window) == 4,
    all(complete.cases(
      log_biomass_future,
      log_biomass_t,
      log_bees,
      precip_t,
      precip_future_spring
    ))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  distinct(year, ecosystem)

sph_model_data <- sph_model_data %>%
  semi_join(complete_pairs, by = c("year", "ecosystem")) %>%
  mutate(
    precip_t_z = as.numeric(scale(precip_t)),
    precip_future_spring_z =
      as.numeric(scale(precip_future_spring))
  )

# 2. Compare windows with leave-one-year-out cross-validation
# Cross-validation function
cv_window <- function(dat, include_bees = TRUE) {

  years <- sort(unique(dat$future_year))

  predictions <- map_dfr(years, function(yr) {

    train <- dat %>% filter(future_year != yr)
    test  <- dat %>% filter(future_year == yr)

    formula <- if (include_bees) {
      log_biomass_future ~
        log_biomass_t +
        log_bees +
        precip_t_z +
        precip_future_spring_z +
        factor(ecosystem)
    } else {
      log_biomass_future ~
        log_biomass_t +
        precip_t_z +
        precip_future_spring_z +
        factor(ecosystem)
    }

    fit <- lm(formula, data = train)

    test %>%
      mutate(
        predicted = predict(fit, newdata = test)
      )
  })

  predictions %>%
    summarise(
      RMSE = sqrt(mean(
        (log_biomass_future - predicted)^2
      )),
      MAE = mean(abs(log_biomass_future - predicted))
    )
}

# Baseline (without bees)
baseline <- sph_model_data %>%
  filter(window == "full") %>%
  cv_window(include_bees = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(window = "no_bees")

# Four candidate windows
window_results <- sph_model_data %>%
  group_by(window) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ cv_window(.x, include_bees = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Compare
cv_results <- bind_rows(
  baseline,
  window_results
) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

cv_results


# 3. Plot predictive performance
ggplot(
  cv_results,
  aes(x = reorder(window, RMSE), y = RMSE)
) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "Bee abundance window",
    y = "Cross-validated RMSE",
    title = "Predicting next-year Sphaeralcea biomass"
  )
```

The midseason window (June–August) performs best, but the improvement over the model without bees is small.

What this tells us
- Midseason bees improve prediction slightly: RMSE decreases by approximately 2.1% relative to the baseline model.
- Full-season bees provide essentially no improvement.
- Early- and late-season bees perform worse than the baseline.

```{r}
# 4. Next: Examine the year-by-year predictive improvement

mid_dat <- sph_model_data %>%
  filter(window == "mid")

cv_predictions <- map_dfr(
  sort(unique(mid_dat$future_year)),
  function(yr) {

    train <- mid_dat %>% filter(future_year != yr)
    test  <- mid_dat %>% filter(future_year == yr)

    baseline_fit <- lm(
      log_biomass_future ~
        log_biomass_t +
        precip_t_z +
        precip_future_spring_z +
        factor(ecosystem),
      data = train
    )

    bee_fit <- lm(
      log_biomass_future ~
        log_biomass_t +
        log_bees +
        precip_t_z +
        precip_future_spring_z +
        factor(ecosystem),
      data = train
    )

    test %>%
      mutate(
        pred_baseline = predict(baseline_fit, newdata = test),
        pred_bees = predict(bee_fit, newdata = test),
        sq_error_baseline =
          (log_biomass_future - pred_baseline)^2,
        sq_error_bees =
          (log_biomass_future - pred_bees)^2
      )
  }
)

year_performance <- cv_predictions %>%
  group_by(future_year) %>%
  summarise(
    RMSE_baseline = sqrt(mean(sq_error_baseline)),
    RMSE_bees = sqrt(mean(sq_error_bees)),
    improvement = RMSE_baseline - RMSE_bees,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  year_performance,
  aes(x = future_year, y = improvement)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4A90C3") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Plant biomass year",
    y = "Reduction in RMSE",
    title = "Does midseason bee abundance improve biomass prediction?",
    subtitle = "Positive values indicate improved prediction"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

year_performance
```

The seasonal abundance of Sphaeralcea-associated bees differs substantially among ecosystems. So let's use the full-season (March–October) bee abundance as the primary predictor, with early-, mid-, and late-season abundance as secondary analyses.


Does the abundance of bees recorded visiting Sphaeralcea predict changes in Sphaeralcea biomass over the following 1–3 years, after accounting for precipitation and existing biomass?
```{r}
# Compare 1-, 2-, and 3-year lags

# Full-season bee abundance
bee_annual <- bee_windows %>%
  filter(window == "full") %>%
  select(year, ecosystem, bee_abundance)

# Spring Sphaeralcea biomass
sph_annual <- plant_season %>%
  filter(
    plant_group == "Sphaeralcea",
    season == "spring"
  ) %>%
  select(
    year, ecosystem,
    biomass = mean_plant_biomass
  )

# Construct datasets for 1-, 2-, and 3-year lags
sph_lags <- map_dfr(1:3, function(lag_years) {

  bee_annual %>%
    left_join(
      sph_annual,
      by = c("year", "ecosystem")
    ) %>%
    rename(biomass_t = biomass) %>%
    mutate(
      lag = lag_years,
      future_year = year + lag_years
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      sph_annual %>%
        rename(
          future_year = year,
          biomass_future = biomass
        ),
      by = c("future_year", "ecosystem")
    )
})

# Inspect sample sizes and years
lag_coverage <- sph_lags %>%
  group_by(lag) %>%
  summarise(
    n_observations = sum(
      !is.na(biomass_t) & !is.na(biomass_future)
    ),
    n_years = n_distinct(
      year[!is.na(biomass_t) & !is.na(biomass_future)]
    ),
    first_bee_year = min(
      year[!is.na(biomass_t) & !is.na(biomass_future)]
    ),
    last_bee_year = max(
      year[!is.na(biomass_t) & !is.na(biomass_future)]
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

lag_coverage


# Prepare a consistent modeling dataset

# Restrict all lags to the same bee years
sph_lags_common <- sph_lags %>%
  filter(
    year %in% 2002:2015,
    !is.na(biomass_t),
    !is.na(biomass_future)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    log_biomass_t = log1p(biomass_t),
    log_biomass_future = log1p(biomass_future),
    log_bees = log1p(bee_abundance)
  )

# Verify observations and response years - looks good (42 obs per lag)
sph_lags_common %>%
  group_by(lag) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_bee_years = n_distinct(year),
    first_response_year = min(future_year),
    last_response_year = max(future_year),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Calculate precipitation for each bee year, ecosystem, and lag
precip_lags <- sph_lags_common %>%
  distinct(year, ecosystem, lag, future_year) %>%
  mutate(
    
    # We're using cumulative precipitation
    precip_cumulative = pmap_dbl(
      list(year, ecosystem, lag, future_year),
      function(year, ecosystem, lag, future_year) {

        p <- precip_wide %>%
          filter(
            .data$ecosystem == .env$ecosystem,
            .data$year >= .env$year,
            .data$year <= .env$future_year
          ) %>%
          arrange(.data$year)

        # Require all years and seasonal values
        if (
          nrow(p) != lag + 1 ||
          anyNA(p$precip_spring) ||
          anyNA(p$precip_fall)
        ) {
          return(NA_real_)
        }

        # Fall of initial year
        total <- p$precip_fall[1]

        # Complete intervening years
        if (lag > 1) {
          total <- total +
            sum(p$precip_t[2:lag])
        }

        # Spring of response year
        total + p$precip_spring[lag + 1]
      }
    )
  )

# Join precipitation to the modeling data
sph_lags_model <- sph_lags_common %>%
  left_join(
    precip_lags,
    by = c("year", "ecosystem", "lag", "future_year")
  )


# Step 2. Check the results
sph_lags_model %>%
  group_by(lag) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    missing_precip = sum(is.na(precip_cumulative)),
    min_precip = min(precip_cumulative, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_precip = mean(precip_cumulative, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_precip = max(precip_cumulative, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

1. Fit the lagged biomass models

Each model will test whether full-season abundance of bees recorded visiting Sphaeralcea predicts subsequent Sphaeralcea biomass, controlling for initial biomass, cumulative precipitation, and ecosystem.

We'll standardize precipitation separately within each lag because the cumulative totals represent different time intervals. Also use the same bee predictor scale across all three models so the bee coefficients are directly comparable.
```{r}
library(purrr)
library(broom)

# Prepare predictors
sph_lags_model <- sph_lags_model %>%
  group_by(lag) %>%
  mutate(
    precip_z = as.numeric(scale(precip_cumulative))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    ecosystem = factor(ecosystem),
    log_bees = log1p(bee_abundance)
  )

# Fit one model per lag
lag_models <- sph_lags_model %>%
  split(.$lag) %>%
  map(~ lm(
    log_biomass_future ~
      log_biomass_t +
      log_bees +
      precip_z +
      ecosystem,
    data = .x
  ))

# Extract bee coefficients and confidence intervals
bee_effects <- imap_dfr(
  lag_models,
  ~ tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == "log_bees") %>%
    mutate(lag = as.integer(.y))
) %>%
  select(lag, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, p.value)

bee_effects


# Plot how the bee association changes with lag
ggplot(
  bee_effects,
  aes(x = lag, y = estimate)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
    width = 0.12
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3) +
  labs(
    x = "Lag between bee abundance and plant biomass (years)",
    y = "Bee coefficient (95% CI)",
    title = "Association between bee abundance and future Sphaeralcea biomass"
  )
```


Test whether the one-year association is robust to shared year effects. A useful sensitivity analysis is to add bee-year fixed effects. This asks whether ecosystems with relatively higher bee abundance in a given year also have relatively higher subsequent biomass, after controlling for initial biomass, precipitation, and ecosystem.
```{r}
# One-year lag only
dat_1yr <- sph_lags_model %>%
  filter(lag == 1) %>%
  mutate(year = factor(year))

# Original model
m_original <- lag_models[["1"]]

# Model accounting for shared year effects
m_year <- lm(
  log_biomass_future ~
    log_biomass_t +
    log_bees +
    precip_z +
    ecosystem +
    year,
  data = dat_1yr
)

# Compare bee coefficients
bind_rows(
  tidy(m_original, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == "log_bees") %>%
    mutate(model = "Original"),
  tidy(m_year, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == "log_bees") %>%
    mutate(model = "Year fixed effects")
) %>%
  select(model, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, p.value)
```

The estimated association actually becomes stronger, but less precise

Do specialist bee fluctuations predict subsequent plant biomass?

```{r}
  filter(lag == 1) %>%
  select(-log_bees) %>%

    specialist_annual,
```

Do specialist bees predict subsequent plant biomass better than generalist bees?
```{r}
### Construct the generalist bee predictor

# Identify polylectic bees associated with Sphaeralcea
sph_generalists <- bee_diets %>%
  filter(
    Diet.Breadth == "Polylectic",
    grepl("Sphaeralcea", Floral.partner.s.)
  ) %>%
  pull(Code) %>%
  unique()

# Calculate annual abundance
generalist_annual <- bee.data %>%
  filter(
    !year %in% c(2016, 2017),
    complete_sampling_month == 1
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    generalist_count = rowSums(
      across(all_of(intersect(sph_generalists, names(bee.data)))),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, ecosystem) %>%
  summarise(
    generalist_abundance = mean(generalist_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Add generalist abundance to the specialist model dataset
sph_compare <- sph_specialist_model %>%
  left_join(generalist_annual, by = c("year", "ecosystem")) %>%
  mutate(
    log_generalists = log1p(generalist_abundance),
    specialists_z = as.numeric(scale(log_specialists)),
    generalists_z = as.numeric(scale(log_generalists))
  )


### Fit comparable models

m_spec <- lm(
  log_biomass_future ~
    log_biomass_t + specialists_z + precip_z + ecosystem,
  data = sph_compare
)

m_gen <- lm(
  log_biomass_future ~
    log_biomass_t + generalists_z + precip_z + ecosystem,
  data = sph_compare
)

# Compare standardized bee effects
bind_rows(
  tidy(m_spec, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == "specialists_z") %>%
    mutate(group = "Specialists"),
  tidy(m_gen, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term == "generalists_z") %>%
    mutate(group = "Generalists")
) %>%
  select(group, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, p.value)
```

Longitudinal model of annual changes in Sphaeralcea biomass, with specialist bee abundance in the preceding year as the predictor.
```{r}
### Prepare the dataset

dat <- sph_specialist_model %>%
  mutate(
    ecosystem = factor(ecosystem),
    year = as.integer(year)
  ) %>%
  group_by(ecosystem) %>%
  mutate(
    bee_anomaly = log_specialists -
      mean(log_specialists, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(ecosystem, year)

# Check the dataset
dat %>%
  group_by(ecosystem) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bee_anomaly = mean(bee_anomaly),
    sd_bee_anomaly = sd(bee_anomaly),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


### Fit the primary model
m_primary <- lm(
  log_biomass_future ~
    log_biomass_t +
    bee_anomaly +
    precip_z +
    ecosystem,
  data = dat
)

summary(m_primary)
confint(m_primary, "bee_anomaly")


### Account for shared annual variation

library(clubSandwich)

clubSandwich::coef_test(
  m_primary,
  vcov = "CR2",
  cluster = dat$year,
  test = "Satterthwaite"
)


### Test whether bee fluctuations explain plant fluctuations

# Model without bees
m_null <- lm(
  log_biomass_future ~
    log_biomass_t +
    precip_z +
    ecosystem,
  data = dat
)

# Additional explanatory power of specialist bees
r2_null <- summary(m_null)$r.squared
r2_bees <- summary(m_primary)$r.squared

data.frame(
  R2_without_bees = r2_null,
  R2_with_bees = r2_bees,
  Delta_R2 = r2_bees - r2_null
)


### Visualize

# Residualize plant biomass against covariates
plant_resid <- residuals(m_null)

# Residualize bee anomalies against the same covariates
m_bee_resid <- lm(
  bee_anomaly ~
    log_biomass_t +
    precip_z +
    ecosystem,
  data = dat
)

plot_dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    plant_resid = plant_resid,
    bee_resid = residuals(m_bee_resid)
  )

ggplot(
  plot_dat,
  aes(x = bee_resid, y = plant_resid)
) +
  geom_point(aes(color = ecosystem), size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Specialist bee abundance (adjusted anomaly)",
    y = "Subsequent Sphaeralcea biomass (adjusted)",
    title = "Specialist bee fluctuations and subsequent plant biomass"
  ) 
```

# Another method

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)

# ============================================================
# 1. Build annual plant-bee dataset
# ============================================================

plant_dat <- sph_annual %>%
  select(year, ecosystem, biomass)

bee_dat <- specialist_annual %>%
  select(year, ecosystem, specialist_abundance)

# Create a complete annual plant series for each ecosystem.
# Keep only consecutive-year transitions with bee observations.

dat <- plant_dat %>%
  left_join(bee_dat, by = c("year", "ecosystem")) %>%
  left_join(
    precip_wide %>%
      select(year, ecosystem, precip_fall),
    by = c("year", "ecosystem")
  ) %>%
  arrange(ecosystem, year) %>%
  group_by(ecosystem) %>%
  mutate(
    next_year = lead(year),
    biomass_next = lead(biomass),
    precip_next_spring = NA_real_
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-precip_next_spring) %>%
  left_join(
    precip_wide %>%
      transmute(
        next_year = year,
        ecosystem,
        precip_next_spring = precip_spring
      ),
    by = c("next_year", "ecosystem")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    next_year == year + 1,
    !is.na(specialist_abundance),
    !is.na(biomass),
    !is.na(biomass_next),
    !is.na(precip_fall),
    !is.na(precip_next_spring)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ecosystem = factor(ecosystem),
    log_plant = log1p(biomass),
    log_plant_next = log1p(biomass_next),
    log_bees = log1p(specialist_abundance),
    precip_interval = precip_fall + precip_next_spring
  )

# Match the previously analyzed 2002-2015 period.
# This avoids the incomplete bee sampling years and the
# isolated 2018-2019 transition.
dat <- dat %>%
  filter(year %in% 2002:2015)

# Center bee abundance within ecosystems
dat <- dat %>%
  group_by(ecosystem) %>%
  mutate(
    bee_anomaly = log_bees - mean(log_bees)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    precip_z = as.numeric(scale(precip_interval))
  )

# Verify coverage
dat %>%
  count(ecosystem)


# ============================================================
# 2. Fit dynamic biomass model
# ============================================================

m <- lm(
  log_plant_next ~
    log_plant +
    bee_anomaly +
    precip_z +
    ecosystem,
  data = dat
)

summary(m)

# Account for shared conditions among ecosystems within years
library(clubSandwich)

coef_test(
  m,
  vcov = "CR2",
  cluster = dat$year,
  test = "Satterthwaite"
)


# ============================================================
# 3. Simulate plant trajectories with and without bee
#    fluctuations
# ============================================================

simulate_trajectory <- function(model, data, use_bees = TRUE) {

  data <- data %>%
    arrange(year)

  simulated <- numeric(nrow(data) + 1)

  # Begin at observed initial biomass
  simulated[1] <- data$log_plant[1]

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(data))) {

    newdat <- data[i, , drop = FALSE]

    # Use simulated previous biomass
    newdat$log_plant <- simulated[i]

    if (!use_bees) {
      newdat$bee_anomaly <- 0
    }

    simulated[i + 1] <- as.numeric(
      predict(model, newdata = newdat)
    )
  }

  tibble(
    year = c(data$year[1], data$next_year),
    predicted_log_biomass = simulated
  )
}

# Simulate each ecosystem
trajectories <- split(dat, dat$ecosystem) %>%
  imap_dfr(function(d, eco) {

    with_bees <- simulate_trajectory(m, d, TRUE) %>%
      mutate(scenario = "Observed bee fluctuations")

    constant_bees <- simulate_trajectory(m, d, FALSE) %>%
      mutate(scenario = "Constant bee abundance")

    bind_rows(with_bees, constant_bees) %>%
      mutate(ecosystem = eco)
  })


# ============================================================
# 4. Compare temporal variability
# ============================================================

variance_results <- trajectories %>%
  group_by(ecosystem, scenario) %>%
  summarise(
    temporal_variance = var(predicted_log_biomass),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = scenario,
    values_from = temporal_variance
  ) %>%
  rename(
    variance_with_bees = `Observed bee fluctuations`,
    variance_constant_bees = `Constant bee abundance`
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    variance_difference =
      variance_with_bees - variance_constant_bees,
    percent_difference =
      100 * variance_difference / variance_constant_bees
  )

variance_results


# ============================================================
# 5. Visualize simulated trajectories
# ============================================================

ggplot(
  trajectories,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = predicted_log_biomass,
    color = scenario
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ ecosystem) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Predicted log(1 + Sphaeralcea biomass)",
    color = NULL,
    title = "Predicted Sphaeralcea biomass trajectories",
    subtitle = "With observed versus constant specialist bee abundance"
  ) 

```

# Another another method

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(clubSandwich)

# ============================================================
# 1. Calculate annual changes in specialist bee abundance
# ============================================================

bee_changes <- specialist_annual %>%
  filter(year %in% 2002:2015) %>%
  arrange(ecosystem, year) %>%
  group_by(ecosystem) %>%
  mutate(
    log_bees = log1p(specialist_abundance),

    bee_change = log_bees - lag(log_bees),

    # Only calculate changes between consecutive years
    bee_change = if_else(
      year - lag(year) == 1,
      bee_change,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(year, ecosystem, bee_change)


# ============================================================
# 2. Join bee changes to subsequent plant biomass changes
# ============================================================

# Existing dat has:
# log_plant = log biomass in year t
# log_plant_next = log biomass in year t+1
# precip_z = standardized precipitation between censuses

change_dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    plant_change = log_plant_next - log_plant
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    bee_changes,
    by = c("year", "ecosystem")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(bee_change),
    !is.na(plant_change),
    !is.na(precip_z)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ecosystem = factor(ecosystem)
  )

# Check sample sizes
change_dat %>%
  group_by(ecosystem) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    first_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# ============================================================
# 3. Visualize the relationship
# ============================================================

ggplot(
  change_dat,
  aes(
    x = bee_change,
    y = plant_change,
    color = ecosystem
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Annual change in log(1 + specialist bee abundance)",
    y = "Subsequent change in log(1 + Sphaeralcea biomass)",
    title = "Do specialist bee fluctuations precede plant fluctuations?"
  ) +
  theme_classic()


# ============================================================
# 4. Fit the first-difference model
# ============================================================

m_change <- lm(
  plant_change ~
    bee_change +
    precip_z +
    ecosystem,
  data = change_dat
)

summary(m_change)


# ============================================================
# 5. Account for shared annual conditions
# ============================================================

change_test <- coef_test(
  m_change,
  vcov = "CR2",
  cluster = change_dat$year,
  test = "Satterthwaite"
)

change_test


# ============================================================
# 6. Compare models with and without bees
# ============================================================

m_change_null <- lm(
  plant_change ~
    precip_z +
    ecosystem,
  data = change_dat
)

r2_comparison <- tibble(
  R2_without_bees = summary(m_change_null)$r.squared,
  R2_with_bees = summary(m_change)$r.squared
) %>%
  mutate(
    Delta_R2 = R2_with_bees - R2_without_bees
  )

r2_comparison


# ============================================================
# 7. Leave-one-year-out cross-validation
# ============================================================

cv_change <- map_dfr(
  sort(unique(change_dat$year)),
  function(yr) {

    train <- change_dat %>%
      filter(year != yr)

    test <- change_dat %>%
      filter(year == yr)

    model_without <- lm(
      plant_change ~ precip_z + ecosystem,
      data = train
    )

    model_with <- lm(
      plant_change ~ bee_change + precip_z + ecosystem,
      data = train
    )

    tibble(
      year = yr,
      ecosystem = test$ecosystem,
      observed = test$plant_change,
      predicted_without = predict(
        model_without,
        newdata = test
      ),
      predicted_with = predict(
        model_with,
        newdata = test
      )
    )
  }
)

cv_change_summary <- cv_change %>%
  summarise(
    RMSE_without_bees = sqrt(
      mean((observed - predicted_without)^2)
    ),
    RMSE_with_bees = sqrt(
      mean((observed - predicted_with)^2)
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent_improvement =
      100 * (RMSE_without_bees - RMSE_with_bees) /
      RMSE_without_bees
  )

cv_change_summary


# ============================================================
# 8. Plot observed vs predicted plant changes
# ============================================================

ggplot(
  cv_change,
  aes(
    x = observed,
    y = predicted_with,
    color = ecosystem
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "Observed change in Sphaeralcea biomass",
    y = "Cross-validated predicted change",
    title = "Predicting plant biomass changes from specialist bees"
  )
```

# Sphaeralcae count data

```{r}
count_data <- read.csv("./data/sev330_NPP_quad_cover_height.csv")

sph_codes <- c("SPHA", "SPHAE", "SPLE")

# All sampled quadrats, not just those containing Sphaeralcea
sampled <- count_data %>%
  filter(
    site %in% c("core_blue", "core_black", "core_creosote"),
    year %in% 2002:2016,
    season == 2
  ) %>%
  distinct(year, site, quadID)

# Sum Sphaeralcea counts within quadrats
sph_counts <- count_data %>%
  filter(
    site %in% c("core_blue", "core_black", "core_creosote"),
    year %in% 2002:2016,
    season == 2,
    species %in% sph_codes
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, site, quadID) %>%
  summarise(
    sph_count = sum(count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Add zero counts for sampled quadrats without Sphaeralcea
sph_count_quad <- sampled %>%
  left_join(sph_counts, by = c("year", "site", "quadID")) %>%
  mutate(
    sph_count = replace_na(sph_count, 0),
    ecosystem = case_when(
      site == "core_blue" ~ "B",
      site == "core_black" ~ "G",
      site == "core_creosote" ~ "C"
    )
  )

# Annual abundance and occupancy
sph_count_annual <- sph_count_quad %>%
  group_by(year, ecosystem) %>%
  summarise(
    n_quads = n(),
    total_count = sum(sph_count),
    mean_count = mean(sph_count),
    occupancy = mean(sph_count > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(sph_count_annual, n = Inf)
```

Spring vs. fall counts
```{r}
### 1. Calculate annual spring and fall plant counts
sph_codes <- c("SPHA", "SPHAE", "SPLE")

# All sampled quadrats in blue grama grassland
sampled_B <- count_data %>%
  filter(
    site == "core_blue",
    year %in% 2002:2016,
    season %in% c(2, 3)
  ) %>%
  distinct(year, season, quadID)

# Sphaeralcea counts per quadrat
sph_counts_B <- count_data %>%
  filter(
    site == "core_blue",
    year %in% 2002:2016,
    season %in% c(2, 3),
    species %in% sph_codes
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, season, quadID) %>%
  summarise(
    sph_count = sum(count),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Include zeros and calculate annual means
sph_season_annual <- sampled_B %>%
  left_join(
    sph_counts_B,
    by = c("year", "season", "quadID")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sph_count = replace_na(sph_count, 0),
    season = recode(
      as.character(season),
      "2" = "spring",
      "3" = "fall"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(year, season) %>%
  summarise(
    n_quads = n(),
    total_count = sum(sph_count),
    mean_count = mean(sph_count),
    occupancy = mean(sph_count > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(sph_season_annual, n = Inf)


### 2. Plot spring and fall abundance
ggplot(
  sph_season_annual,
  aes(x = year, y = mean_count, color = season)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("spring" = "#4A90C3", "fall" = "#D55E5E")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Mean Sphaeralcea count per quadrat",
    color = "Season"
  ) 


### 3. Fit the same bee model separately for each season

# Construct lagged plant abundance
dat_season <- sph_season_annual %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    count_next = lead(mean_count),
    next_year = lead(year)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(next_year == year + 1) %>%
  left_join(
    specialist_annual %>%
      filter(ecosystem == "B") %>%
      select(year, specialist_abundance),
    by = "year"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    dat %>%
      filter(ecosystem == "B") %>%
      select(year, precip_interval),
    by = "year"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(specialist_abundance),
    !is.na(precip_interval)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    log_count = log1p(mean_count),
    log_count_next = log1p(count_next),
    log_bees = log1p(specialist_abundance),
    precip_z = as.numeric(scale(precip_interval))
  )

# Fit separate models
m_spring <- lm(
  log_count_next ~ log_count + log_bees + precip_z,
  data = filter(dat_season, season == "spring")
)

m_fall <- lm(
  log_count_next ~ log_count + log_bees + precip_z,
  data = filter(dat_season, season == "fall")
)

summary(m_spring)
summary(m_fall)


### 4. Compare bee coefficients and sensitivity to 2015

compare_models <- function(data, season_name) {

  d <- filter(data, season == season_name)

  full <- lm(
    log_count_next ~ log_count + log_bees + precip_z,
    data = d
  )

  without_2015 <- lm(
    log_count_next ~ log_count + log_bees + precip_z,
    data = filter(d, year != 2015)
  )

  tibble(
    season = season_name,
    model = c("All years", "Exclude 2015"),
    n = c(nobs(full), nobs(without_2015)),
    bee_coefficient = c(
      coef(full)["log_bees"],
      coef(without_2015)["log_bees"]
    ),
    bee_p = c(
      coef(summary(full))["log_bees", "Pr(>|t|)"],
      coef(summary(without_2015))["log_bees", "Pr(>|t|)"]
    ),
    adjusted_R2 = c(
      summary(full)$adj.r.squared,
      summary(without_2015)$adj.r.squared
    )
  )
}

bind_rows(
  compare_models(dat_season, "spring"),
  compare_models(dat_season, "fall")
)
```

```{r}
  data = dat_plant_bee_climate
)

m_bees_biomass_climate <- lm(
  log_bees ~ log_biomass + precip_z,
  data = dat_plant_bee_climate
)

summary(m_bees_count_climate)
summary(m_bees_biomass_climate)


m_bees_count_climate_no2015 <- lm(
  log_bees ~ log_count + precip_z,
  data = filter(dat_plant_bee_climate, year != 2015)
)

m_bees_biomass_climate_no2015 <- lm(
  log_bees ~ log_biomass + precip_z,
  data = filter(dat_plant_bee_climate, year != 2015)
)

summary(m_bees_count_climate_no2015)
summary(m_bees_biomass_climate_no2015)
```
